result:
The proposed answer, λ, is wrong. Since λ can be any positive real number, λ can exceed 1, but a probability cannot.

The correct limit is e^{-λ}. A k×n generator matrix defines an MDS code exactly when every k of its n columns are linearly independent. There are C(n,k) such k-subsets. For k random vectors in 𝔽_q^k, the chance of linear dependence is 1/q + O(1/q²). So the expected number of dependent k-subsets is about C(n,k)/q → λ. When k/n → 0, these dependencies are weak enough for a Poisson approximation to hold, giving P(MDS) → e^{-λ}. I did not verify the Poisson step in detail, and I am recalling the result from the literature rather than deriving it fully here.

The proposed solution also gives no justification for the step from the normalization to the answer λ. It only asserts it.

VERDICT: REJECT

CONFIDENCE: 4
